subject: mathematics
question_text: The vectors AB = 3i − 2j + 2k and AD = i − 2k represent adjacent sides of a parallelogram ABCD. Find the angle between the diagonals.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.105 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 162. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's own inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: classed SAQ on its length and shape. The bank prints no mark cut, so this classification is OURS. Printed appearances: TS 18. Both diagonals must be written in terms of the two GIVEN sides first. In parallelogram ABCD the vertices go round in order, so BC equals AD — that is the fact that unlocks AC. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular split for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

steps.label: Find the diagonal AC
steps.margin_note: First mark. AC = AB + BC, and in a parallelogram BC = AD because those two sides are equal and parallel.
lines: Diagonal AC = AB + BC = AB + AD

recall.must_convey: That AC = AB + AD = 4i − 2j, using BC = AD.
accept: A C is A B plus A D because B C equals A D, giving four i minus two j
the first diagonal is the sum of the two sides
A C comes to four i minus two j
A C ante A B plus A D, four i minus two j

steps.why: The k components cancel exactly here (2k − 2k), so AC has no k part. Write the result as 4i − 2j rather than 4i − 2j + 0k.
common_mistakes: Using AB + BC without noticing BC = AD.
Adding the k components instead of cancelling them.

steps.label: Find the diagonal BD
steps.margin_note: Second mark. AB + BD = AD, so BD = AD − AB. The order matters: it is the far end minus the near end.
lines: AB + BD = AD ⇒ BD = AD − AB

accept: B D is A D minus A B which gives minus two i plus two j minus four k
the second diagonal is the difference of the two sides
B D comes to minus two i plus two j minus four k
B D ante A D minus A B

steps.why: The two diagonals are the SUM and the DIFFERENCE of the adjacent sides. Getting the difference the wrong way round reverses BD and gives the supplementary angle.
common_mistakes: Dropping a minus sign while subtracting.

steps.label: Apply the cos formula
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. cos θ = (AC·BD)/(|AC||BD|). The dot product is negative, so the answer is an obtuse angle — that is correct, not a slip.

recall.must_convey: That cos θ = (AC·BD)/(|AC||BD|) = −√3/√10, so θ = Cos⁻¹(−√3/√10).
accept: the dot product is minus twelve, the lengths are two root five and two root six, giving cos theta minus root three over root ten
apply the cosine formula and simplify
theta is cos inverse of minus root three by root ten
cos theta minus root three by root ten
the angle is obtuse because the cosine is negative

steps.why: A negative cosine means the angle between the two diagonals as written is obtuse. The acute angle between the same two lines is its supplement.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign to make the answer look tidier.
Forgetting the zero k component of AC in the dot product.
